objects.description: Signed integer type resulting from pointer subtraction. This header provides a typedef to long for ptrdiff_t only for WinCE when it is not already defined. Details like exact width may vary by platform; here it aliases long.

No custom structs, enums, typedefs, or classes are defined in this header. It only contains preprocessor macros for versioning and a compile-time consistency check. Therefore, there is no user-defined type to document.

objects.definition: typedef void *GC_PTR; /*< preserved only for backward compatibility */
objects.description: Legacy alias for void*. Preserved for backward compatibility with older Boehm GC clients.

Unsigned machine word type used by the GC; same width as size_t/addresses. Underlying base macro GC_UNSIGNEDWORD is expected to be an unsigned integral type. Exact width depends on platform configuration.
Signed machine word type used by the GC; same width as ptrdiff_t/addresses. Underlying base macro GC_SIGNEDWORD is a signed integral type. Exact width depends on platform configuration.
Unsigned integer type capable of holding a pointer value. It aliases to system uintptr_t when available (except certain Cygwin/MSYS cases), otherwise to GC_word.
Version value type returned by GC_get_version(). Not defined in this header; defined in included headers (gc_version.h). Omitted per instruction, but referenced here for clarity.
Function pointer type for out-of-memory handler. Called with requested byte size; may return NULL or a valid previously-allocated pointer. Must not be NULL as a variable value when set.
Callback type invoked when the heap grows or shrinks; called with world stopped and allocator lock held.

objects.definition:
typedef enum {
  GC_EVENT_START, /*< start collection */
  GC_EVENT_MARK_START,
  GC_EVENT_MARK_END,
  GC_EVENT_RECLAIM_START,
  GC_EVENT_RECLAIM_END,
  GC_EVENT_END,              /*< end collection */
  GC_EVENT_PRE_STOP_WORLD,   /*< begin stopping world */
  GC_EVENT_POST_STOP_WORLD,  /*< end stopping world */
  GC_EVENT_PRE_START_WORLD,  /*< begin restarting world */
  GC_EVENT_POST_START_WORLD, /*< end restarting world */
  GC_EVENT_THREAD_SUSPENDED,
  GC_EVENT_THREAD_UNSUSPENDED
} GC_EventType;
objects.description: Enumeration of collector progress and thread suspend/resume events reported to client callbacks.
Callback type for general GC collection progress notifications (excluding thread suspend/resume).
Callback invoked by collector when there are objects to be finalized (at most once per GC cycle) in on-demand mode.
Callback type used by debug pointer-checking to report errors regarding pointer validity/visibility.
Callback type used by debug pointer-checking to report non-aliasing of two pointers to same object.
Portable time structure with millisecond and nanosecond parts used for incremental GC time limits and performance metrics.

objects.definition:
#if (defined(GC_CAN_SAVE_CALL_STACKS) || defined(GC_ADD_CALLER)) \
    && !defined(GC_RETURN_ADDR_T_DEFINED)
#  if defined(__GNUC__)
typedef void *GC_return_addr_t;
#  else
typedef void (*GC_return_addr_t)(void);
#  endif
#  define GC_RETURN_ADDR_T_DEFINED
#endif /* GC_CAN_SAVE_CALL_STACKS || GC_ADD_CALLER */
objects.description: Type to hold a function return address for debugging/call-stack capture. Defined conditionally based on build macros. As data pointer under GCC to avoid warnings.
Callback type used to abort a GC when it returns nonzero; passed to GC_try_to_collect and as default stop function.
Snapshot structure of various GC profiling/statistics counters. Used with GC_get_prof_stats and GC_get_prof_stats_unsafe.
Client finalizer function type invoked with object and client data when object becomes unreachable according to selected policy.
Enumeration describing the desired state of a toggle-ref managed object: drop tracking, strong ref, or weak ref.
Callback queried by GC to decide the new toggle-ref state of a registered object. Called with allocator lock held.
Callback invoked for each unreachable object enqueued for finalization. Set/get via GC_set_await_finalize_proc/GC_get_await_finalize_proc.
Warning reporting function type used by the collector for diagnostics; message is printf-like format string with one uintptr argument.
Fatal abort callback type invoked before process termination on GC fatal errors. Must be non-NULL.
Integer type used to disguise pointers for finalization safety. Macros hide/reveal by bitwise inversion; special NZ variant also provided elsewhere.
Generic function type used with GC_call_with_alloc_lock, GC_call_with_reader_lock, GC_do_blocking, GC_call_with_gc_active. Returns a void* result and takes a void* client_data.
Holds the cold-end (bottom) addresses of a thread's stack(s). On IA-64/e2k, includes a separate register stack base.
Function type used by GC_call_with_stack_base to supply a captured stack base to a client function.
Filter callback to decide whether a discovered dynamic library section should be scanned as a static root. Return nonzero to scan.
Enumeration describing types of heap sections/blocks used for debugging dumps and iteration.
Callback applied to heap sections/blocks by GC_foreach_heap_section_inner during debugging iteration.

objects.definition: /* None: no struct/enum/typedef/class is defined in this header. */
objects.description: This header defines inline/macro allocation helpers and declares several functions and macros for the Boehm-Demers-Weiser GC fast path. It does not introduce any new user-defined types (no structs, enums, typedefs, or classes). All types appearing here (e.g., size_t, void, GC_word) are either built-ins or declared in other headers (gc.h, gc_tiny_fl.h).

Opaque mark-stack entry structure used by the GC marker. In client builds (neither GC_BUILD nor NOT_GCBUILD), it is defined as a single opaque pointer field; otherwise it is an incomplete type. Instances represent entries on the GC mark stack passed between marking APIs.

Opaque heap-block descriptor used by the collector to represent a heap block. In client builds it is defined as a single opaque pointer field; otherwise it is an incomplete type. Used in callbacks that iterate or query heap blocks.

Function-pointer type for client-supplied mark procedures. Called by the GC to push additional work on the mark stack; returns the new mark-stack pointer. The addr argument should be treated as a pointer to a void*; env carries client data.
Callback function type applied to each allocated heap block by GC_apply_to_all_blocks. Receives a heap-block handle and client data.
Callback function type applied to each completely empty heap block by GC_iterate_free_hblks. Receives the block and its free-list index.
Callback type that produces a human-readable description for an object, used by debug support when printing objects. Buffer length is GC_TYPE_DESCR_LEN.
Callback type invoked at the start of every full collection when registered via GC_set_start_callback.
Callback type for client-provided routine that pushes additional root sets during marking. Set/get via GC_set_push_other_roots/GC_get_push_other_roots.
Callback type used by GC_enumerate_reachable_objects_inner to visit all reachable objects; receives object base, size, and client data.
Callback type invoked when the mark stack becomes empty, allowing clients to push additional work (e.g., for ephemerons). Set/get via GC_set_on_mark_stack_empty/GC_get_on_mark_stack_empty.
Alias for a pointer to GC_word used as a bitmap describing which pointer-sized words within an object may contain pointers. Each bit corresponds to a pointer-sized slot.
Type descriptor token (machine word) describing the pointer layout of an object or array elements. Obtained from GC_make_descriptor and passed to typed allocation calls.

An opaque, precomputed description used to efficiently allocate multiple typed arrays with the same layout and element count. Clients treat it as an opaque blob; content and invariants are internal to the GC. Prepare with GC_calloc_prepare_explicitly_typed and use with GC_calloc_do_explicitly_typed.

Pointer-to-function type for disclaim callbacks invoked by the GC with the allocator lock held. The function takes a single void* to the object and returns nonzero to keep the object for this cycle, zero to allow reclamation. Calling convention and attributes are given by GC_CALLBACK. Details about GC_CALLBACK are not defined here.

Closure object bundling a finalization function and its client data used by GC_finalized_malloc. The proc member is a GC_finalization_proc (defined elsewhere) and cd is an arbitrary client data pointer. Instances are typically stack- or heap-allocated by the user and passed by pointer to GC_finalized_malloc.

Enumeration of reference kinds used by the back-pointer API to describe how a destination address is reachable: unreferenced, not from debug space, from a root, from a register, from another heap object, or via finalizer reachability. Used as the return type of GC_get_back_ptr_info to classify the source of a reference.

objects.definition:
GC_API int GC_gcj_kind;
GC_API int GC_gcj_debug_kind;
objects.description: Global kind identifiers used internally by the Boehm GC to tag normal and debug GCJ-allocated objects. These are integers exported by the library and are primarily useful for debug support and introspection. Construction and lifetime are managed by the GC; user code should not assign to them except via the GC internals.

Opaque cord string handle. Implemented as const char* for compatibility; NULL represents the empty cord. Non-empty literal C strings are valid CORDs if not modified. Mutating underlying C strings after inclusion in a CORD is forbidden.

Function pointer type mapping an index i to a character; used to build functional cords with CORD_from_fn. Implementations must be pure with respect to the underlying cord content and valid for indices in [0,len).
Callback invoked for each character during iteration (forward or reverse). Return nonzero to terminate traversal.
Callback invoked for contiguous C-string substrings during iteration to optimize repeated per-char calls. Return nonzero to terminate. Use CORD_NO_FN to disable.
Out-of-memory handler callback type. A global variable CORD_oom_fn (if declared) and accessor functions control the handler. Zero means default abort behavior.
Internal path entry used in CORD position state. Holds a reference to a cord node and the start index within that node. Private implementation detail but layout is exposed for macros.

Opaque-ish position handle for iterating over a CORD. The typedef defines CORD_pos as a single-element array of struct CORD_Pos, so a CORD_pos behaves like a pointer to a struct when passed to APIs/macros. It tracks current index, cached leaf substring, and a path stack into the rope for efficient next/prev and fetching.

An extensible cord handle used as a single-element array of a struct holding an accumulated cord (ec_cord) and a small character buffer (ec_buf) with current write pointer (ec_bufptr). It represents the concatenation of ec_cord with the pending characters in ec_buf. Intended to be stack-allocated and initialized with CORD_ec_init, appended to with CORD_ec_append or CORD_ec_append_cord, and converted to a CORD via CORD_ec_to_cord (which flushes the buffer). Destruction is trivial; no explicit free is required beyond any management inherent to the CORD members. The underlying CORD type is declared in cord.h and not defined here.

No custom data types are defined in this header. It only includes another header (gc/gc.h) for backward compatibility. Types referenced in the included header are out of scope per the instructions and are therefore ignored.

functions.name: GC_get_version
functions.description: Return the collector library version as a constant: (major << 16) | (minor << 8) | micro. Intended for runtime checking of the linked GC library version.

functions.name: GC_get_gc_no
functions.description: Return the current GC cycle number (increments once per collection, including early empty collections). Unsynchronized getter; primarily for stats/monitoring.
requirements: Caller should use GC_call_with_reader_lock() if accessing from multiple threads to avoid data races.

functions.name: GC_get_parallel
functions.description: Return the number of marker threads minus one (0 if single-threaded). Does not acquire the allocator lock.

functions.name: GC_set_markers_count
functions.description: Set desired total number of marker threads (including the initiating one) at startup. Has no effect after GC initialization and does not create threads itself.
requirements: Must be called before the collector is initialized.
Passing 0 lets the collector decide the count.
Function is unsynchronized; avoid racing with initialization.

functions.name: GC_set_oom_fn
functions.description: Set the callback invoked when an allocation cannot be satisfied. If the function returns, it must return either NULL or a valid pointer to a previously allocated heap object.
requirements: Argument must be non-NULL.
Callback must either return NULL or a valid pointer previously allocated by the GC.
Setter acquires the allocator lock; no extra locking required by caller.

functions.name: GC_get_oom_fn
functions.description: Get the current out-of-memory callback used by the collector.
requirements: Getter acquires the allocator lock (reader mode); no extra locking required by caller.

functions.name: GC_set_on_heap_resize
functions.description: Set a callback to be invoked when the heap grows or shrinks. Called by GC with the world stopped and allocator lock held. May be NULL to disable.
requirements: Callback may be NULL.
Callback will be called with allocator lock held and possibly world-stopped; it must not perform operations that require GC functions that could recurse improperly.

functions.name: GC_get_on_heap_resize
functions.description: Get the current heap-resize callback (may be NULL).
requirements: Getter acquires the allocator lock (reader mode).

functions.name: GC_set_on_collection_event
functions.description: Set a callback notified on GC progress events (start/end, mark/reclaim phases, world-stop transitions). Not used for thread suspend/resume notifications. May be NULL to disable.
requirements: Callback may be NULL.
Callback is called with allocator lock held (and possibly world-stopped).

functions.name: GC_get_on_collection_event
functions.description: Get the current collection-event callback (may be NULL).
requirements: Getter acquires the allocator lock (reader mode).

functions.name: GC_set_on_thread_event
functions.description: Set a callback invoked when a thread is suspended or resumed during collection. Available only when built with GC_THREADS. May be NULL to disable.
requirements: Available only if the collector is built with GC_THREADS.
Callback may be NULL.
Callback is called with allocator lock held (and world partially stopped).

functions.name: GC_get_on_thread_event
functions.description: Get the current thread-event callback (may be NULL). Available only when built with GC_THREADS.
requirements: Available only if the collector is built with GC_THREADS.
Getter acquires the allocator lock (reader mode).

functions.name: GC_set_find_leak
functions.description: Enable or disable find-leak mode. In this mode GC does not reclaim memory but reports inaccessible memory not explicitly freed. Initial value from FIND_LEAK. Typically not modified after initialization; only supported if built without NO_FIND_LEAK.

functions.name: GC_get_find_leak
functions.description: Get the current find-leak mode flag.

functions.name: GC_set_all_interior_pointers
functions.description: Enable/disable recognition of interior pointers as valid references. Changing after initialization is possible but setter acquires the allocator lock. Affects off-the-end pointer recognition depending on configuration.

functions.name: GC_get_all_interior_pointers
functions.description: Get the current interior-pointer recognition mode flag.

functions.name: GC_set_finalize_on_demand
functions.description: Set whether finalizers run only when GC_invoke_finalizers() is called explicitly (on-demand). Default derives from FINALIZE_ON_DEMAND. Unsynchronized.

functions.name: GC_get_finalize_on_demand
functions.description: Get the on-demand finalization flag. Unsynchronized.

functions.name: GC_set_java_finalization
functions.description: Enable/disable Java-style finalization semantics (mark objects reachable from finalizable ones in a post-pass). Required for GC_register_finalizer_unreachable to work correctly. Unsynchronized.

functions.name: GC_get_java_finalization
functions.description: Get the Java-style finalization flag. Unsynchronized.

functions.name: GC_set_finalizer_notifier
functions.description: Set a callback invoked by GC when finalizable objects are enqueued and GC_finalize_on_demand is set. Called at most once per collection cycle. May be NULL to disable. Setter acquires allocator lock.
requirements: Callback may be NULL.
Callback is invoked with allocator lock held.

functions.name: GC_get_finalizer_notifier
functions.description: Get the current finalizer notifier callback (may be NULL).
requirements: Getter acquires the allocator lock (reader mode).

functions.name: GC_set_same_obj_print_proc
functions.description: Set the print handler used by GC_same_obj() failure reporting. Must not be NULL. Unsynchronized.
requirements: Argument must be non-NULL.
Handler will be called without the allocator lock held.

functions.name: GC_get_same_obj_print_proc
functions.description: Get the current same-object print handler.

functions.name: GC_set_is_valid_displacement_print_proc
functions.description: Set the print handler used by GC_is_valid_displacement() failure reporting. Must not be NULL. Unsynchronized.
requirements: Argument must be non-NULL.
Handler will be called without the allocator lock held.

functions.name: GC_get_is_valid_displacement_print_proc
functions.description: Get the current valid-displacement print handler.

functions.name: GC_set_is_visible_print_proc
functions.description: Set the print handler used by GC_is_visible() failure reporting. Must not be NULL. Unsynchronized.
requirements: Argument must be non-NULL.
Handler will be called without the allocator lock held.

functions.name: GC_get_is_visible_print_proc
functions.description: Get the current visibility check print handler.

functions.name: GC_set_dont_expand
functions.description: Set the flag to prevent heap expansion unless explicitly requested or forced. Unsynchronized.

functions.name: GC_get_dont_expand
functions.description: Get the current no-heap-expansion flag. Unsynchronized.

functions.name: GC_set_full_freq
functions.description: Set the number of partial collections between full, world-stopped collections. Intended for tuning when incremental mode is enabled.
requirements: Unsynchronized setter: if the program has entered multi-threaded mode, callers should wrap this with GC_call_with_alloc_lock() to avoid data races.
Value meaning is implementation-defined; typical values in the tens are reasonable.

functions.name: GC_get_full_freq
functions.description: Get the current setting of the number of partial collections between full collections.
requirements: Unsynchronized getter: in multi-threaded use, call under GC_call_with_reader_lock() to avoid data races.

functions.name: GC_set_non_gc_bytes
functions.description: Set the number of bytes that are not considered candidates for collection (used for scheduling). Wizards-only tuning hook.
requirements: Unsynchronized setter: in multi-threaded mode, call under GC_call_with_alloc_lock() to avoid data races.

functions.name: GC_get_non_gc_bytes
functions.description: Get the number of bytes not considered candidates for collection.
requirements: Unsynchronized getter: in multi-threaded mode, call under GC_call_with_reader_lock() to avoid data races.

functions.name: GC_set_no_dls
functions.description: Control automatic registration of dynamic library data segments as roots. Nonzero disables auto-registration (wizards only).
requirements: Should be set only if the client registers all roots explicitly.
Unsynchronized setter.

functions.name: GC_get_no_dls
functions.description: Get whether automatic dynamic library data segment registration is disabled.
requirements: Unsynchronized getter.

functions.name: GC_set_free_space_divisor
functions.description: Set GC_free_space_divisor, a tuning parameter controlling space/time trade-off between collections.
requirements: Unsynchronized setter: in multi-threaded mode, call under GC_call_with_alloc_lock() to avoid data races.

functions.name: GC_get_free_space_divisor
functions.description: Get GC_free_space_divisor, which affects collection frequency vs. memory usage.
requirements: Unsynchronized getter: in multi-threaded mode, call under GC_call_with_reader_lock() to avoid data races.

functions.name: GC_set_max_retries
functions.description: Set the maximum number of collection attempts after a failed heap expansion before reporting OOM.
requirements: Unsynchronized setter: in multi-threaded mode, call under GC_call_with_alloc_lock() to avoid data races.

functions.name: GC_get_max_retries
functions.description: Get the maximum number of collection retries after expansion failure.
requirements: Unsynchronized getter: in multi-threaded mode, call under GC_call_with_reader_lock() to avoid data races.

functions.name: GC_set_dont_precollect
functions.description: Set the flag to skip collection during GC initialization (wizards only).
requirements: Should be set only before initialization for intended effect.
Unsynchronized setter (accessed at init only).

functions.name: GC_get_dont_precollect
functions.description: Get the flag that controls pre-collection during initialization.
requirements: Unsynchronized getter.

functions.name: GC_set_time_limit
functions.description: Set the soft time limit (milliseconds) for incremental collections; GC_TIME_UNLIMITED disables pause checks.
requirements: Unsynchronized setter: in multi-threaded mode, call under GC_call_with_alloc_lock() to avoid data races.
Setter does not modify the nanosecond component; use GC_set_time_limit_tv() to set ns part.

functions.name: GC_get_time_limit
functions.description: Get the incremental collection time limit (milliseconds).
requirements: Unsynchronized getter: in multi-threaded mode, call under GC_call_with_reader_lock() to avoid data races.

functions.name: GC_set_time_limit_tv
functions.description: Set the incremental collection time limit with millisecond and nanosecond precision.
requirements: tv_nsec must be less than 1000000.
If tv_ms equals GC_TIME_UNLIMITED, tv_nsec is ignored.
No synchronization used.

functions.name: GC_get_time_limit_tv
functions.description: Get the incremental collection time limit with nanosecond precision.
requirements: No synchronization used.

functions.name: GC_set_allocd_bytes_per_finalizer
functions.description: Set the min ratio of allocated bytes to number of finalizers created since last GC; affects collection vs expansion decision (non-incremental mode).
requirements: Zero disables finalizer-count influence.
No synchronization used.

functions.name: GC_get_allocd_bytes_per_finalizer
functions.description: Get the current allocated-bytes-per-finalizer threshold.
requirements: No synchronization used.

functions.name: GC_start_performance_measurement
functions.description: Start internal performance measurements of collection times.
requirements: No synchronization used.
Available only if library built without NO_CLOCK.

functions.name: GC_get_full_gc_total_time
functions.description: Return total time (ms) spent in full collections since measurements began.
requirements: No synchronization used.
Value wraps on overflow.
Available only if built without NO_CLOCK.

functions.name: GC_get_stopped_mark_total_time
functions.description: Return total time (ms) spent in world-stopped mark phases since measurements began.
requirements: No synchronization used.
Available only if built without NO_CLOCK.

functions.name: GC_get_avg_stopped_mark_time_ns
functions.description: Return average time (nanoseconds) for world-stopped mark phases since measurements began or initialization if logging enabled.
requirements: Acquires allocator lock (reader mode).
Available only if built without NO_CLOCK.

functions.name: GC_set_pages_executable
functions.description: Control whether GC allocates executable memory pages (nonzero enables). Must be called before GC initialization.
requirements: Must be called before collector initialization for effect.
May have no effect on some platforms.

functions.name: GC_get_pages_executable
functions.description: Return whether the GC will allocate pages with execute permission.
requirements: No synchronization used.

functions.name: GC_set_min_bytes_allocd
functions.description: Set the minimum value returned by internal min_bytes_allocd(); default is 1 and must not be zero.
requirements: Argument must be nonzero.
Not synchronized.

functions.name: GC_get_min_bytes_allocd
functions.description: Get the configured minimum bytes for internal min_bytes_allocd().
requirements: Not synchronized.

functions.name: GC_set_rate
functions.description: Set size in pages for GC_collect_a_little() work units; must be nonzero.
requirements: Argument must be nonzero.
Not synchronized.

functions.name: GC_get_rate
functions.description: Get the page unit size used by GC_collect_a_little().
requirements: Not synchronized.

functions.name: GC_set_max_prior_attempts
functions.description: Set the maximum number of prior attempts at world-stop marking.
requirements: Not synchronized.

functions.name: GC_get_max_prior_attempts
functions.description: Get the maximum number of prior world-stop marking attempts.
requirements: Not synchronized.

functions.name: GC_set_disable_automatic_collection
functions.description: Enable or disable the heuristic that triggers GC when enough has been allocated to amortize collection.
requirements: Acquires allocator lock (writer).

functions.name: GC_get_disable_automatic_collection
functions.description: Query whether automatic collection trigger is disabled.
requirements: Acquires allocator lock (reader).

functions.name: GC_set_handle_fork
functions.description: Override default fork-handling mode. Nonzero requests installing pthread_atfork handlers at initialization; -1 selects manual atfork API usage.
requirements: Must be called before collector initialization for effect.
May cause abort at initialization if pthread_atfork is missing or fails.

functions.name: GC_atfork_prepare
functions.description: Manual atfork handler to call immediately before fork() if not handled automatically.
requirements: Should be paired with GC_atfork_parent() and GC_atfork_child() around fork().
May be called from unregistered threads.

functions.name: GC_atfork_parent
functions.description: Manual atfork handler to call in the parent branch immediately after fork().
requirements: Use only in combination with GC_atfork_prepare/child around fork().

functions.name: GC_atfork_child
functions.description: Manual atfork handler to call in the child branch immediately after fork().
requirements: Call before any GC_start_mark_threads() in the child.

functions.name: GC_init
functions.description: Initialize the Boehm GC. Portable clients should instead call GC_INIT() from main().
requirements: Safe to call multiple times.
Some platforms require call from primordial thread.

functions.name: GC_is_init_called
functions.description: Return nonzero if the collector is initialized or initialization is in progress.

functions.name: GC_deinit
functions.description: Shutdown the collector (e.g., free OS-specific resources). Duplicate calls are no-ops.
requirements: On Windows, typically call GC_win32_free_heap() before this.

functions.name: GC_malloc
functions.signature: GC_API GC_ATTR_MALLOC GC_ATTR_ALLOC_SIZE(1) void *GC_CALL GC_malloc(size_t /* size_in_bytes */);
functions.description: Allocate a traced, zero-initialized, collectable object of the given size. Never returns NULL unless GC_oom_fn returns NULL.
requirements: size_in_bytes may be zero (semantics implementation-defined).

functions.name: GC_malloc_atomic
functions.signature: GC_API GC_ATTR_MALLOC GC_ATTR_ALLOC_SIZE(1) void *GC_CALL GC_malloc_atomic(size_t /* size_in_bytes */);
functions.description: Allocate an atomic (pointer-free) collectable object; contents are not scanned for pointers. Never returns NULL unless GC_oom_fn returns NULL.

functions.name: GC_strdup
functions.description: Duplicate a C string into GC-managed memory. Never returns NULL unless GC_oom_fn returns NULL.
requirements: Argument should be a valid, NUL-terminated string.

functions.name: GC_strndup
functions.signature: GC_API GC_ATTR_MALLOC char *GC_CALL GC_strndup(const char *, size_t) GC_ATTR_NONNULL(1);
functions.description: Duplicate up to n characters of a C string into GC-managed memory. Never returns NULL unless GC_oom_fn returns NULL.
requirements: First argument must be non-NULL.

functions.name: GC_malloc_uncollectable
functions.signature: GC_API GC_ATTR_MALLOC GC_ATTR_ALLOC_SIZE(1) void *GC_CALL GC_malloc_uncollectable(size_t /* size_in_bytes */);
functions.description: Allocate an uncollectible object that is scanned for pointers but not itself reclaimed. Never returns NULL unless GC_oom_fn returns NULL.

functions.name: GC_memalign
functions.signature: GC_API GC_ATTR_MALLOC GC_ATTR_ALLOC_SIZE(2) void *GC_CALL GC_memalign(size_t /* align */, size_t /* lb */);
functions.description: Allocate a collectable object with a specified alignment. Never returns NULL unless GC_oom_fn returns NULL.
requirements: align must be nonzero and a power of two.

functions.name: GC_posix_memalign
functions.signature: GC_API int GC_CALL GC_posix_memalign(void ** /* memptr */, size_t /* align */, size_t /* lb */) GC_ATTR_NONNULL(1);
functions.description: Allocate aligned memory like POSIX posix_memalign, primarily for leak-finding redirection. On failure, returns nonzero and does not modify *memptr.
requirements: memptr must be non-NULL.
align must be nonzero, a power of two, and not less than sizeof(void*).

functions.name: GC_valloc
functions.signature: GC_API GC_ATTR_MALLOC GC_ATTR_ALLOC_SIZE(1) void *GC_CALL GC_valloc(size_t /* lb */);
functions.description: Allocate a page-aligned object (valloc-like). Never returns NULL unless GC_oom_fn returns NULL.
requirements: Available only if GC_NO_VALLOC is not defined.

functions.name: GC_pvalloc
functions.signature: GC_API GC_ATTR_MALLOC GC_ATTR_ALLOC_SIZE(1) void *GC_CALL GC_pvalloc(size_t /* lb */);
functions.description: Allocate page-aligned memory sized to a page multiple (pvalloc-like). Never returns NULL unless GC_oom_fn returns NULL.
requirements: Available only if GC_NO_VALLOC is not defined.

functions.name: GC_free
functions.description: Explicitly deallocate a GC-allocated object. Dangerous if used incorrectly.
requirements: Argument may be NULL (no-op).
Pointer must be to the base of an object.
Object must not have a registered finalizer or disappearing links when freed.

functions.name: GC_debug_free
functions.description: Debug variant of GC_free that checks for overwrites and debug headers.
requirements: Same as GC_free.

functions.name: GC_freezero

functions.name: GC_get_dont_add_byte_at_end

requirements: May be meaningfully interpreted only if GC_get_all_interior_pointers() returns 1; otherwise the value is not relevant.

functions.name: GC_generic_malloc_many
functions.signature: GC_API void GC_CALL GC_generic_malloc_many(size_t lb_adjusted, int kind, void **result);
functions.description: Batch-allocates one or more objects of the specified adjusted size and returns them as a singly-linked free list via *result, with the list linked through the first pointer-sized field in each object. Intended to reduce allocator lock contention by acquiring the lock once and populating a thread-local free list.
requirements: lb_adjusted must be nonzero.
lb_adjusted must be a multiple of GC_GRANULE_BYTES.
lb_adjusted must already include any extra byte required for all-interior-pointers mode unless GC_get_dont_add_byte_at_end() returns nonzero.
kind must be a valid object kind (e.g., GC_I_NORMAL or GC_I_PTRFREE).
result must be a non-NULL pointer to a location where the head of the list will be stored.
The client must ensure that *result is traced/reachable even if the objects are pointer-free (GC_I_PTRFREE), otherwise the collector may reclaim the list.
The client should usually clear the link field in each returned object before use.
This routine does not acquire the allocator lock per returned object; typical usage is to replenish a thread-local free list.
Multi-threaded clients should include atomic_ops.h (or similar) before this header (as noted by the API comments).
Manual use is discouraged; primarily intended for compiler-generated code and internal thread-local allocation.

functions.name: GC_malloc_kind
functions.signature: GC_API GC_ATTR_MALLOC GC_ATTR_ALLOC_SIZE(1) void *GC_CALL GC_malloc_kind(size_t lb, int kind);
functions.description: Allocates a single object of lb bytes using the free list of the specified kind. This is the generalized form of GC_malloc (for traced objects) and GC_malloc_atomic (for pointer-free objects), selecting the allocation strategy by kind.
requirements: lb is the requested size in bytes (no explicit lower/upper bounds specified here).
kind must be a valid object kind (e.g., GC_I_NORMAL for traced objects, GC_I_PTRFREE for pointer-free).

If all-interior-pointers mode is in effect and GC_get_dont_add_byte_at_end() returns 0, callers that need one-past-the-end safety are responsible for adding an extra byte to lb (per header’s general warning).
The returned pointer has allocation semantics consistent with the specified kind (pointer-containing vs pointer-free).
On allocation failure, behavior is determined by the collector’s OOM handler (not specified here).

functions.name: GC_malloc_kind_global
functions.signature: GC_API GC_ATTR_MALLOC GC_ATTR_ALLOC_SIZE(1) void *GC_CALL GC_malloc_kind_global(size_t lb, int kind);
functions.description: Same as GC_malloc_kind but explicitly allocates using only the global free list (no thread-local fast path). Provided as a function when GC_THREADS is defined; otherwise this name is a macro alias of GC_malloc_kind.
requirements: Available as a distinct function only when GC_THREADS is defined; otherwise GC_malloc_kind_global is a macro that resolves to GC_malloc_kind with identical arguments and behavior.
lb is the requested size in bytes.
kind must be a valid object kind (e.g., GC_I_NORMAL or GC_I_PTRFREE).

If all-interior-pointers mode is in effect and GC_get_dont_add_byte_at_end() returns 0, callers that need one-past-the-end safety are responsible for adding an extra byte to lb (per header’s general warning).

functions.description: Debug helper that prints the addresses of each object in the free list for the given kind and size class lg (in granules). Intended for diagnostics and debugging builds.
requirements: kind must be a valid object kind.

requirements: Unsynchronized: may race with concurrent setter; guard externally if needed.

functions.name: GC_mark_and_push

obj should be the base address expected by the descriptor.
